clue.text: Conservative running angry London area

blocks.note: C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative
haring means running fast, like a hare
cross means annoyed

explanation.surface: A Tory candidate is out campaigning in a furious mood across a part of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Charing Cross is a district and major railway terminus in central London, near Trafalgar Square.

clue.text: Showing sound judgment, authorised housing site, we hear

indicators.note: housing means holding something inside, so one word goes within the other
we hear tells the solver to go by how the word is spoken rather than spelt

blocks.note: cleared means given official permission
a word pronounced just like site but meaning vision

explanation.surface: A planning approval for a building site seems a sensible decision, or so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone clear-sighted sees situations accurately, so they display good, perceptive judgment.

clue.text: Weapon of old, small in breadth, top missing

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the first letter, and missing says it is dropped

blocks.note: narrow means of small width

explanation.surface: An ancient weapon, slim in profile, has lost its tip.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrow, shot from a bow, was a principal missile weapon in medieval warfare.

clue.text: One showing little emotion presenting lettuce

blocks.note: first meaning: a cold, unemotional person
second meaning: a crisp, pale variety of salad leaf

explanation.surface: An impassive person deadpan hands over a salad leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: The person sense is figurative: someone as cold as floating ice.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a crisp salad variety and, informally, a frosty, unresponsive person.

clue.text: Willing to hide billion pounds — risky venture

indicators.note: hiding something means keeping it inside, so letters go within the first word

blocks.note: game means ready and eager to do something
B is an abbreviation for billion
L, from Latin libra, stands for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: Being prepared to conceal a billion pounds is a dangerous undertaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamble is an action whose outcome is uncertain, taken in hope of gain despite danger.

clue.text: Give a light tint to some hair in session

indicators.note: some means only a portion, so the answer is a stretch inside the following words

blocks.note: runs from the end of hair across in into the start of session

explanation.surface: A hairdresser colours a client's hair slightly during an appointment.
explanation.definitionFit: A rinse is a temporary hair dye, so to rinse hair is to tint it lightly.

clue.text: Purist upset, making case for right riding equipment

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are jumbled
a case surrounds its contents, so the jumbled word encloses the next letter

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A disgruntled stickler argues for the correct horse-riding kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A stirrup is the loop hanging from a saddle that supports the rider's foot, part of riding tack.

clue.text: Contest where Equus has no realistic rival?

definitions.text: Contest where Equus has no realistic rival?

blocks.clueFragment: Contest where Equus has no realistic rival?
blocks.note: surface reading: a competition dominated by one overwhelming favourite
setter's reading: Equus is Latin for horse, so picture a lone horse with nobody worth racing against

explanation.surface: A competition in which a horse called Equus faces no serious challenger.
explanation.walkthrough: Equus is the genus name for horses; the idiom is used of any contest with a foregone winner.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes any competition so lopsided that only a single entrant has a real chance.

clue.text: Always missing venue initially, that is weird

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so a letter is taken out of the first word
initially points to the opening letter of the word beside it

blocks.note: ever means always, as in ever hopeful
first letter of venue
i.e. is the abbreviation of Latin id est, that is

explanation.surface: It is strange that the venue is always absent at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie and weird are synonyms, both meaning strange in an unsettling, uncanny way.

clue.text: House guy and child with one inside

indicators.note: inside says the single letter is placed within the preceding word

blocks.note: a guy is a man
a son is a male child
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A household made up of a man and his child, with one more person living there.
explanation.definitionFit: A mansion is a large, grand house, so it is a specific kind of dwelling.

clue.text: Untreated timber — that's unfair treatment

blocks.note: raw means unprocessed
deal is fir or pine wood

explanation.surface: Being sold untreated wood is a poor bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal, a soft pine or fir timber, is chiefly a British word.
explanation.definitionFit: A raw deal is an idiom for being treated unjustly or harshly.

clue.text: Fireside area, no longer hot, where we live

indicators.note: no longer says something has gone, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: the hearth is the floor of a fireplace
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: The fireplace has gone cold in the home we live in.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is our planet, the home of humankind, described cryptically by its residents.

clue.text: Challenge as false, troublemaker, fudging on regular basis

indicators.note: regular means at even intervals, so only every other letter is kept

blocks.note: an imp is a mischievous person
second, fourth and sixth letters of fudging

explanation.surface: Someone disputes the honesty of a mischief-maker who keeps dodging the truth.
explanation.definitionFit: To impugn a claim is to dispute its truth or question its validity.

clue.text: Garden feature, leapfrog, organised after female leaves

indicators.note: organised means put into a new order, so the letters are rearranged
leaves means goes away, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: taken as written
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A game of leapfrog in the garden is set up once a woman departs.
explanation.definitionFit: A pergola is an arched framework over a path for climbing plants, a common garden structure.

clue.text: Daze Proust's written about?

indicators.note: about suggests letters turned around and set down in a different arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wry question: is drowsy confusion what Marcel Proust's long novel describes?
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is' joining definition to wordplay; the question mark nods to Proust's famously soporific prose.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a state of near-unconsciousness or bewilderment, essentially a daze.

clue.text: Maybe unworthily take trophy (not half!) supported by employer

indicators.note: not half says only part of the word is kept, the rest being discarded

blocks.note: taken as written
a user is one who employs something

explanation.surface: Pocketing a trophy without merit, backed by one's boss.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'supported by' puts the second piece below the first. Trouser is British slang for pocketing money, often dishonestly.
explanation.definitionFit: To trouser money is informal British usage for taking it into one's pocket, often undeservedly.

clue.text: Complain over extremely explicit reprimand

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the outermost letters of the next word

blocks.note: to carp is to grumble
first and last letters of explicit

explanation.surface: Grumbling about a very blunt telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'over' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is informal for summoning them to be scolded, from being called onto the boss's carpet.

clue.text: Wading bird, one admired at start of November

indicators.note: start of points to the opening letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: a hero is someone admired
first letter of November

explanation.surface: A wading bird draws admirers in early November.
explanation.definitionFit: The heron is a long-legged bird that stands in shallow water to catch fish.

clue.text: Even up, embracing Republican — that shows courage

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the word is read from bottom to top
embracing means holding within, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: Levelling the score by hugging a Republican is a brave move.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve means boldness or daring, a synonym for courage.

clue.text: A job with the French Christian missionary

blocks.note: taken as written
a post is a position of employment
le is French for the; with simply joins

explanation.surface: A position held with a French employer by a Christian missionary.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostle is one of Christ's original followers sent out to preach, or any early Christian missionary.

clue.text: Monotonously repeat part of myth, rumour

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a portion lying within the following words

blocks.note: runs from the end of myth into the start of rumour

explanation.surface: Someone drones on, retelling a bit of legend and gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrum is to drum or strum with a steady, monotonous sound, as in repeating tediously.

clue.text: Act of self-gratification, pert — I go mad

indicators.note: mad means wild and disordered, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cheeky person confesses that self-indulgence drives them crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego trip is an activity done chiefly to boost one's own self-importance.

clue.text: Leaders of society you recall in anguished country

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so the opening letter of each word is taken

blocks.note: first letters of the five words

explanation.surface: Prominent figures of society remember a land in distress.
explanation.definitionFit: Syria is a nation in the Middle East, making it an instance of a country.

clue.text: I need change from computer work — I'm sure about that!

definitions.text: I need change from computer work

blocks.clueFragment: I need change from computer work
blocks.note: first meaning, read cryptically: remove IT, information technology, from me
second meaning: a phrase vouching for what one says

explanation.surface: A fed-up office worker insists they need a break from screens, and they mean it.
explanation.walkthrough: IT is information technology; the first half reads the phrase literally as a plea to have computer work taken off one's hands.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom asserting that the speaker can be believed, much like saying trust me.
